name: RRB NTPC (Railway Recruitment)
summary: Non-Technical Popular Categories recruitment exam for graduate and undergraduate posts across Indian Railways, including Station Master, Goods Guard, and Clerk roles.
eligibility: Undergraduate posts: passed Class 12 (10+2) from a recognised board
Graduate posts: bachelor's degree from a recognised university, plus typing proficiency in English or Hindi for some posts
Age limits vary by post, typically 18-33 years with category-based relaxation
documents: Passport-size photograph and signature per RRB specification
fee: ₹500 for General/OBC/EWS candidates (₹400 refunded after appearing for CBT 1); ₹250 for women, SC, ST, and other exempted categories (fully refunded after appearing for CBT 1).
process: Notification released separately by RRB zones for Graduate and Undergraduate levels
Apply online through the relevant regional RRB website
Appear for Computer Based Test 1 (CBT 1), a screening round
Typing skill test or document verification (post-dependent), followed by medical examination
Final merit list and zone/post allocation released

faq.question: Is the RRB NTPC fee refunded?
faq.answer: Partially — General/OBC/EWS candidates get ₹400 refunded (of the ₹500 fee) after appearing for CBT 1, while women, SC, ST, and other exempted categories get a full refund of their ₹250 fee.

faq.question: Do all RRB NTPC posts require the same qualification?
faq.answer: No — undergraduate-level posts need only Class 12, while graduate-level posts require a bachelor's degree. Each notification specifies which posts fall under which level.
